agent_note: Prose fiction, not verse. Cleanest book in the batch: 14 event quotes, all past, third-person free-indirect narration across several named characters (Mia, Pearl, Lexie, Moody). No present-tense narration anywhere on the page. The only present-tense material is two aphorisms (q01500, q01501) and character speech. Worth noting: q01500 and q01520 are the same passage in narration and dialogue form -- a Goodreads near-duplicate that the dedupe step did not catch. Several quotes (q01502, q01513, q01519) use generalized second person but in PAST tense, and a loose 'sounds general' reading would misfile them as gnomic; they are free-indirect thought and are the exact error the methodology warns about. Even so, dropping all three would leave 11 past / 0 present. No single quote can flip this label.
